_comment: Per-score options of `python3 -m pianovision build` (pianovision/buildopts.py). Keys of 'scores' are score
paths relative to the scores folder; keys starting with '_' are comments. Only what build makes of a score
changes, never the score.
title, composer   the song's title and composer (PianoVision's name/artist and the output name)
piano_staves      the staves (1-based) that are the piano part, right hand first; the others are orchestra
hands             'staves' (default) or 'split': the piano part's notes to the hands by pitch and reach
simplified_from   on an orchestral score: a piano solo of the same music (score path); its piano part becomes
the simplified part, measure-aligned, and the song plays on the solo's clock (its tempos)
orchestra_from    on a piano solo: an orchestral score of the same music (score path); its orchestra, measure-
aligned, becomes the song's orchestra, on the solo's clock
measure_map       'auto', or {pin: [[solo, orch], ...], fill: [orch, ...], drop: [solo, ...]} with measures
as the scores number them ('12', '12-30', '395:2' = the second pass): see the report in
<output>/.arrangements/ and `python3 -m pianovision arrangement`
piano_from        'simplified_from' (with simplified_from): the solo is the song's piano part too (Note
Waterfall's original part and PianoVision's hands) wherever the alignment maps a solo
measure; the measures it leaves out keep this score's piano part; no separate simplified
part. Hand edits of the solo's notes go through the solo's own song (`hands review` says so)
song              false: not a song of its own (build retires its output); it can still be another's partner
A partner (simplified_from, orchestra_from) is rendered with its own options here; the companion audio
(`accompaniment`) renders the orchestral score on the solo's clock too (pianovision/timeline.py).

Gershwin/Rhapsody_in_blue__George_Gershw.title: Rhapsody in Blue (Piano and Orchestra)
Gershwin/Rhapsody_in_blue__George_Gershw._title: its own title would collide with the piano solo (gers_Rhapsody_in_Blue.json); its metadata's workTitle says 'Second Rhapsody' (wrong)
Gershwin/Rhapsody_in_blue__George_Gershw._simplified_from: the piano solo arrangement, measure-aligned, gives the song its tempos (the orchestral score's own ending ran too fast); the measures it leaves out play the orchestral score's Solo Piano part, at the orchestral score's own tempo scaled to the solo's next to them
Gershwin/Rhapsody_in_blue__George_Gershw._piano_from: the solo is the source of truth for the piano part (the user, 2026-10-20: errors in the orchestral score's piano part at the ending): the original part and PianoVision's hands are the solo's notes in the 417 orchestral measures it maps (of 522 as played), the orchestral Solo Piano part only in the 105 it leaves out (138-180, 200-254, 256-259, 472-474). At the ending the orchestral score's staves give the wrong hands (383-423 written mostly on the lower staff, 424's L.H./R.H. on swapped staves, 475-480 both hands on the upper staff, 505's run and top octave on the lower), 475-480 sound an octave below the solo (no 8va where the solo has one over both staves) and its 8va lines in 504-507 start and end elsewhere, 401 has A-flat for the B of every other statement; the rest of the ending is different piano writing, the solo folding the orchestra in (425-457, 481-503)

Rachmaninoff/Rhapsody_on_a_theme_of_Paga._orchestra_from: the song is the piano solo (its piano part and tempo) with pagvar18's orchestra, measure-aligned (solo 2-43 = orchestral 1-42), on the solo's clock; the solo's pickup (m. 1) has no orchestra

Rachmaninoff/pagvar18.mscz._song: only the orchestra of the piano solo's song (orchestra_from above); its own song, rach_Rhapsody_on_a_Theme_of_Paganini__Var_XVIII_Piano_and_Orchestra.json, is retired to the attic
Rachmaninoff/pagvar18.mscz._piano: 'Piano, Roland Piano' (staves 11-12) is the solo piano: alone in m. 1-12, about a quarter of its onsets coincide with the orchestra's. The import wrote both hands on staff 11 (clef changes every measure; staff 12 has the overflow), so the hands are split by pitch and reach. 'Piano' (staff 1) holds one stray E-flat 5 in m. 33 doubling the violins: orchestra by its program
